game.title: Pokémon Radical Red
game.revision_note: All device codes here were verified on Radical Red v4.1 (US FireRed 1.0 base). Nothing is verified for v3.02 — treat older RR versions as unsupported. RR also ships its own built-in cheat console (settings → TV in your room) from v4.0.
warnings: Never enable multiple cheats at once — save corruption in Radical Red almost always comes from stacked cheats.
Item cheats deliver via the Item PC, not your bag (RR restructured the item system). Turn them off right after withdrawing.
RR's level caps fight EXP/Rare Candy cheats: over-leveled Pokémon can get stuck earning 1 EXP per battle. Fix: restart the emulator with all cheats disabled.
Generic FireRed codes point at the wrong addresses in RR — don't import them.
Level-modifier cheats don't work in RR, and Gigantamax item codes are dead (that content was removed).
If a code seems inert: enter/exit a building, and double-check the device type — CodeBreaker vs GameShark codes fail silently under the wrong type.

codes.name: Unlimited Rare Candy
codes.description: Withdraw unlimited Rare Candies from any Item PC. Tip: RR also has a built-in cheat console — type Woyaopp on the TV in your room (v4.0+) for infinite Rare Candies with zero corruption risk.
codes.activation: Enable → any Item PC → Withdraw. Turn OFF after withdrawing.
side_effects: Level caps still apply — over-leveling can stall EXP gain at 1 per battle.
Uses the same PC address as the Master Ball code — enable only one at a time.

codes.name: Unlimited Master Ball
codes.description: Withdraw unlimited Master Balls from any Item PC.
codes.activation: Enable → any Item PC → Withdraw. Turn OFF after withdrawing.
side_effects: Uses the same PC address as the Rare Candy code — enable only one at a time.

codes.name: Unlimited Money
codes.description: Max money. A GameShark alternative (29C78059 96542194) and a sell-high option (830050A8 1388, items sell for 5000) also exist on the same source.

codes.name: Walk Through Walls
codes.description: Walk through walls and terrain. The most widely cross-confirmed RR code.
side_effects: Reaching areas early can trigger broken scripting or a softlock — disable before map transitions.

codes.name: Shiny Wild Pokémon
codes.description: Wild encounters are shiny. Note: one source prints a different first line (F3A9A86D 4E2629B4) — this pair is the better-attested RR-specific variant.
codes.activation: Enable, then start a wild encounter
side_effects: Glitched nicknames after catching are a known side effect — turn off when not hunting.

codes.name: Wild Nature Modifier (Adamant)
codes.description: Forces wild Pokémon to Adamant nature. The first line is the required common line; each nature has its own second line (this entry is the Adamant example). Later RR versions also have an in-game mint system.
codes.activation: Enable, then catch the wild Pokémon
side_effects: Only one nature code active at a time.

codes.name: Unlimited EXP
codes.description: Huge EXP after each battle. Sources disagree on device type — enter as CodeBreaker first; if inert, re-enter as GameShark.
codes.activation: Win a battle; turn off to stop gaining
side_effects: Level caps still apply — over-leveled Pokémon stall at 1 EXP per battle.

codes.name: Unlimited PP
codes.description: Party Pokémon never run out of PP in battle.

codes.name: Unlock All Badges
codes.description: All gym badges unlocked (check the trainer card).
codes.activation: Enable, check trainer card, turn off afterwards
side_effects: Badge unlocks interact with obedience mechanics — RR ties obedience to level caps; use with care.

codes.name: Fast Egg Hatch
codes.activation: Enable while walking with an egg; turn off after hatching
